title: What If Every Bat on Earth Vanished?

scenes.text: What if every bat disappeared? In parts of America, a real die-off already hints at the answer.
Since 2006, a fungus called white-nose syndrome has made many North American bat populations collapse.
Where bats crashed, farmers sprayed about thirty-one percent more insecticide on their crops.
A 2024 study in the journal Science followed what happened next.
In those counties, infant deaths rose by almost eight percent. The study links more than thirteen hundred extra deaths to it.
Bats' free pest control protects more than crops. Losing them everywhere would likely hit far beyond America.
